Cause and governing concept: Controls combined operating settings with independently useful Skills and Sites entry points. Strengthen that separation without introducing new APIs or duplicate editors. The runtime intent documents describe the earlier Controls layout; this Goal authorizes the new arrangement, already reflected in the retained worktree documentation.

In index.html, css/base.css, and js/common.js, confirm right-aligned order Skills, Sites, Settings, New Goal; remove duplicate Skills/Sites sections from Settings. Reuse shared summaries, icons, rows, separators, panels, and spacing. Preserve Node/Reporter selectors and existing Settings and creation actions. Confirm mutual exclusion, action/outside-click dismissal, Escape, and keyboard focus behavior.

Task #3 - Verify existing feature ownership. In settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js, retain enabled Custom Skills for the active node and attached-app Sites. Each list must have a separator followed by its New and Manage actions, including empty/error states. Reuse existing creation modals, typed Skill preflight and agent-tab launch, management routes, and published/draft Site URLs. Confirm opening, definition changes, and node changes refresh lists while stale responses cannot replace current entries.

Task #4 - Check language and durable intent. Verify the retained navigation, Skills, Knowledge Hub, toolbar, Guide, and onboarding updates consistently describe Settings and the new entry points. Correct obsolete user-facing Controls references without renaming unrelated internal identifiers.

Task #5 - Verify observable behavior. Run the existing topbar, Knowledge Hub, screen-render, Node navigation, and Skill-terminal browser coverage with Chromium available; skipped tests are not passes. Run the focused Rust static-surface navigation checks. Confirm both themes, narrow/desktop widths, long-list scrolling, reachable action groups, keyboard operation, creation/management destinations, and both draft and published Site opening. Add coverage only for meaningful uncovered behavior.

Task #6 - Resolve the Quality evidence gap. Recover the exact identities and diagnostics of the reported 12 Rust failures and reproduce them against the retained candidate and 9c1be94c using the same environment. Fix regressions caused by this change in their existing owners; document verified baseline failures separately and retain unresolved findings for Quality. Do not weaken tests or infer a complete pass from navigation-only results.

skill.prompt:
## Implementation

Implement the current Goal Round using all accepted plans and attached Skills. Inspect existing code, make the complete change, run appropriate verification, and report evidence for each checklist item. Check the plan's assumptions against the code and keep policy in its shared owner. Prefer one correction that explains the affected behavior over separate fixes at each failing call site. Report evidence-backed plan deviations within the Goal's scope and existing authority. Preserve unrelated changes and historical evidence.

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.

### Semantic code organization

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

If issues outside the Goal’s scope block progress, investigate and fix them or use an evidence-backed workaround, preserving required checks and documenting what you changed.
